newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends down on talk of active seedings.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends down on talk of active seedings.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on talk that corn seedings in the U.S. were active over the weekend and early this week which could boost the total plantings tally "to the upper 30s (37 to 39 percent complete," a trader said.
USDA Monday said 18 percent of the U.S. corn crop had been planted as of Sunday, below 21 percent a year ago but ahead of the 15-percent-five-year average.
However, rainy weather later in the week again stalled corn plantings, especially in the western U.S. Corn Belt, the traders said.
Aggressive selling in the July contract by Refco Inc led the way down, the traders said.
Refco sold five million bushels of July and bought four million bushels of December, they said.

Skepticism surfaced on the trading floor that corn purchased from Argentina had been switched to U.S. origin. But Argentine traders said four major export firms swapped a total of about 600,000 tonnes of corn from Argentine to U.S. origin to supply buyers mainly in South Korea.
Corn closed 1-3/4 to four cents per bushel lower, with May down 3-3/4 at $2.94-3/4. Dec was down 1-3/4 at $2.75-1/2.

The posting of 640,000 bushels of corn for delivery on the May contract and news Continental Grain put out 225,000 bushels of that total also weighed on prices, they said. Also, corn registrations late Friday increased 225,000 bushels, according to the CBOT.
Traders said news U.S. exporters reported a sale of 100,000 tonnes of corn to an unknown destination for 1996-97 delivery helped underpin the market.
A rally in soybeans helped underpin corn futures as did slow farmer selling and mostly firm cash basis markets.

In spread trading, Continental Grain did three million bushels of May/July at 1-1/2 cents, premium May and Farmers Commodities Corp spread one million May/July at 1-1/4 cents, premium May, traders said.
FIMAT Futures bought four million bushels of Dec, Merrill Lynch Futures bought two million Dec, Tenco sold two million July and E.D. and F. Man sold two million July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 67,000 contracts, above the 65,371 traded Thursday.
In corn options, O'Connor and Co bought 400 July $3.00 calls at nine cents and sold 500 December $3.20 calls at 7-1/2 cents, traders said.
O'Connor also bought 300 September $3.40 calls at 4-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, about the same as the 14,355 traded Thursday.
